what: FIRST GENUINE PLANT MEASUREMENT: the rotational dead time is 2.6-3.6 s against a ~1 Hz control period. Both signs, open loop, no controller.
context: First runs after the probe's own report-stream bug was fixed. Read docs/evidence-step-probe-stalled-on-its-own-lease-20260829.md for what the four earlier runs actually measured (nothing).
the_fix_is_confirmed: Both runs: report stream started, continuous started, ready True with no readiness_reason, position_sequence advancing (4->13 and 16->24), 8 and 7 informative intervals. The probe now measures the plant instead of its own lease.
what_is_established: The rotational time constant is SEVERAL TIMES the ~1 Hz control period. A proportional loop at this sample rate cannot be stabilised by tuning -- now measured OPEN LOOP with no controller, on both signs, rather than inferred from a hunting closed loop.
The sign relationship is confirmed open loop: positive angular DECREASES map course, negative INCREASES it, matching docs/toward-tracks-in-place-rotation-20260812.md.
The drivetrain is NOT meaningfully asymmetric: |omega| 4.694 vs 4.147 deg/s, within 12%. That is what running both signs was for.

tau_is_a_LOWER_BOUND.why: Both runs tripped the travel guard, and in run A the course was still changing at the final sample -- the 4 s settle phase did not capture the full decay.
tau_is_a_LOWER_BOUND.run_A_evidence: command went to zero at ~5.0 s and the mower rotated a further 16.99 deg, still turning when the window closed.
tau_is_a_LOWER_BOUND.consequence: tau is AT LEAST 2.6-3.6 s. Do not quote either number as a settled value.

what_this_does_NOT_establish: n = 1 per sign. Two runs is not a distribution.
It does not measure the rotational response as a function of commanded angular -- both runs used |120|, the low end of the measured 120-180 band.
It says nothing about whether a damped or feed-forward controller could work; it only rules out proportional-only at ~1 Hz.
The 2026-08-27 attempt-3 blind travel (0.51 m, n=1, on continuous_motion_window) remains unexplained and is NOT addressed by these runs.

safety.gates: 15 of 15 on both signs before each dispatch
safety.gate_after: enabled false, real_motion_allowed false, verified live API AND RAW [False]

onset_lag_is_the_other_half.finding: Rotation does not START for roughly 1-2 s after the step command, and the PEAK rate occurs at or AFTER the command ends.
onset_lag_is_the_other_half.run_A_plus_120: command open 2.0-5.0 s. Per-interval rates: +2.382 (pre), -2.009, -7.505 (peak, ~1.3-2.3 s after command start), -6.500, -6.529 (~1 s AFTER command zero), -0.645, -2.907.
onset_lag_is_the_other_half.why_it_matters: Onset lag is a separate quantity from the decay constant and is arguably worse for control: the loop issues a correction and NOTHING happens for a full sample period or two. A ~1 Hz proportional loop is therefore commanding into a plant that has not yet responded to the previous command.
onset_lag_is_the_other_half.caveat: The decay is NOT monotonic in either run (-0.645 then -2.907; +6.767 then +1.091). That is chord noise on ~0.26 m chords. It is why tau is taken from the INTEGRAL rather than any per-interval fit, and why no rate law should be fitted to these numbers.
